title: Compatibility snapshot generator and semantic pin policy for VPC IaC
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) customers run a mix of Terraform modules and external providers across versions. Upgrades cause intermittent deployment failures and longer maintenance windows because we lack a single source-of-truth compatibility snapshot, a reproducible pinlist generator, and health-check mapping that ties provider version changes to smoke probes.

Goal: Build an automated compatibility snapshot generator that 1) scans our IaC module set and provider tree, 2) produces a semantic pin policy (major/minor/patch rules + allowed exemptions), and 3) emits a version compatibility matrix CSV/JSON plus health-probe mapping so upgrade playbooks can automatically create canary lanes and rollback rules.
background: We currently maintain multiple ad-hoc pin lists in docs and a couple of internal spreadsheets. Recent incidents (R-2026-02-11) showed a provider minor bump (aws provider 4.x) changed state behavior for VPC attachment resources causing Canary failures across 3 customers. Existing tickets touch long-term pin strategy but do not automate snapshot creation or encode exemption logic. This ticket consolidates those efforts into a reproducible pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible job (CI) that scans all Terraform module manifests and outputs a compatibility snapshot file (JSON + CSV) with provider/version pairs and module constraints.
A semantic-pin policy generator that accepts rules and outputs a pinlist for use in module consumers and our IaC lockfiles.
Health-probe mapping exported that correlates provider changes to the set of smoke probes and canary routes affected.
Automation to create canary lanes in our deployment runbooks from the snapshot (template PR + recommended rollout config).
Security review completed and an audit log of snapshot generation added to the Private control plane runbook.
plan: Prototype scanner that parses module source directories and runs 'terraform providers lock' to collect provider fingerprints.
Design semantic rules DSL: ex. 'pin_minor: allow, pin_patch: true, exempt: resource_glob'.
Implement pinlist generator service (Go) that reads snapshot and rules and emits pinlist and lockfile diffs.
Add mapping between provider-version deltas and our smoke probes (console and agent endpoints) in a JSON config consumed by rollout automation.
Wire job into CI (gha) scheduled weekly and on-module-merge with artifacts pushed to internal storage and a Confluence summary page.
rollout_steps: Run prototype scanner against staging workspace and validate snapshot against known-good spreadsheets.
Create PRs for a small set of internal IaC modules to apply generated pinlist (canary group).
Monitor canary smoke probes for 72 hours. If issues, use produced rollback recipe to revert provider pins.
If canary succeeds, roll forward to remaining modules in two waves with automated PRs and human approvals.
Record final snapshot as the canonical version for the release and tag release artifacts.
health_checks: Provider compatibility smoke probe per provider (aws,gcp,azurerm) that runs resource create/read/destroy cycles.
KV cache sanity probe tied to runtime-1.22 to detect behavior regressions from provider changes.
Deployment drift check comparing applied state with expected plan for canary modules.
Latency SLO verification for private control plane endpoints after module upgrades.
test_matrix_summary: Matrix rows: [module, module_version_constraint, provider, provider_version_range, observed_failures, last_tested_date]. Tests run in a matrix across small/medium/large VPC topologies and recorded to the infra-test dashboard (grafana link in artifacts).
notes: Decision: start with provider-level pinning and add module-level exemptions later to keep scope manageable.
Trade-off: aggressive minor pinning reduces runtime surprises but increases manual churn for security patches; will expose an 'allow-minor' flag per workspace.
Follow-up: integrate with Dedicated autoscaler policies to avoid scheduling upgrades during high-util windows.
Privacy: snapshots will not include customer resource identifiers; they contain only module/provider version metadata.
